title: Where Does Your Fat Go When You Lose Weight?
request: Biku's What's the Catch? Short, used as it is: 'this is the script build for this script' (2026-10-21). The first Short in the new look: drawing at the black-hole bar, the mascot (design 1) blended in (look C), narrator voice 4.
sources: Meerman, R. and Brown, A. J., "When somebody loses weight, where does the fat go?", BMJ, 2014, 349: g7257. 10 kg of fat needs 29 kg of oxygen and becomes 28 kg of carbon dioxide and 11 kg of water; 84% leaves through the lungs, 16% as water; a survey of 150 doctors, dietitians and personal trainers, with the common wrong answers (energy, heat, muscle, faeces). https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.g7257
UNSW press release, "When you lose weight, where does the fat go?", via ScienceDaily, 2014. https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/12/141216212047.htm
AsianScientist, "Where Did The Fat Go?", 2014. Breathing more on its own does not make you lose weight.
NPR, "When You Burn Off That Fat, Where Does It Go?", 2014. The 84% to 16% split; the water leaves as urine, sweat and other body fluids.
Checked by Claude on 2026-10-21: of the 150 asked, only 3 gave the right answer, so "more than half got it wrong" is true and milder than the source; kept as Biku wrote it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When your bathroom scale drops by one kilo of fat, where does that fat actually *go*?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When a hundred and fifty doctors, dietitians and trainers were asked, more than half got it *wrong*.

shots.words: When your bathroom scale drops by one kilo of fat, where does that fat actually *go*?

overlay.text: Where Does Your Fat Go When You Lose Weight?

shots.words: When a hundred and fifty doctors, dietitians and trainers were asked, more than half got it *wrong*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most said it turns into *energy* or heat, and a few said muscle, or the toilet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But fat is made of atoms, and atoms cannot just *vanish*, so let's follow them.

shots.words: Most said it turns into *energy* or heat, and a few said muscle, or the toilet.
But fat is made of atoms, and atoms cannot just *vanish*, so let's follow them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inside your belly, fat sits in tiny fat cells, each one a little bag of *oil*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That oil is built from just three kinds of atoms: carbon, hydrogen and *oxygen*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: To burn that oil, your body needs extra oxygen, which you breathe *in*.

shots.words: Inside your belly, fat sits in tiny fat cells, each one a little bag of *oil*.
That oil is built from just three kinds of atoms: carbon, hydrogen and *oxygen*.
To burn that oil, your body needs extra oxygen, which you breathe *in*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One kilo of fat needs nearly three kilos of oxygen, so your lungs do the heavy *lifting*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your body pulls the oil apart and joins each piece to that *oxygen*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Only two leftovers come out: water, and carbon dioxide, the gas that fizzes in *soda*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That gas slips into your blood and rides it all the way up to your *lungs*.

shots.words: One kilo of fat needs nearly three kilos of oxygen, so your lungs do the heavy *lifting*.
Your body pulls the oil apart and joins each piece to that *oxygen*.
Only two leftovers come out: water, and carbon dioxide, the gas that fizzes in *soda*.
That gas slips into your blood and rides it all the way up to your *lungs*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And then, with your next breath, it floats right out of your *mouth*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Out of every kilo you lose, about eight hundred and forty grams leaves as *breath*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The other hundred and sixty grams becomes water, and leaves as *sweat* and pee.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the gym is really where you go to exhale your *burger*.

shots.words: And then, with your next breath, it floats right out of your *mouth*.
Out of every kilo you lose, about eight hundred and forty grams leaves as *breath*.
The other hundred and sixty grams becomes water, and leaves as *sweat* and pee.
So the gym is really where you go to exhale your *burger*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two scientists in Australia worked this out by tracking every *atom* in ten kilos of fat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ten kilos of fat plus twenty nine kilos of oxygen went *in*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Twenty eight kilos of carbon dioxide and eleven kilos of water came *out*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Both sides weigh thirty nine kilos, so not a single atom went *missing*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And no, panting on the sofa will not burn more fat. You will just get *dizzy*.

shots.words: Two scientists in Australia worked this out by tracking every *atom* in ten kilos of fat.
Ten kilos of fat plus twenty nine kilos of oxygen went *in*.
Twenty eight kilos of carbon dioxide and eleven kilos of water came *out*.
Both sides weigh thirty nine kilos, so not a single atom went *missing*.
And no, panting on the sofa will not burn more fat. You will just get *dizzy*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: From now on, every breath out carries a tiny piece of yesterday's *dinner*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So where did that kilo on your scale go? You breathed it *out*.
